title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock simply because it is cheap, and never chase a Stage 2 leader when it is stretched far above its 10-week moving average; let the tape come back to support where risk is defined.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein — Stage Analysis Principle

web_blocks.html: At the verified November 23, 2026 NSE session close, GRWRHITECH remains in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend [28]. It closed at ₹7,895.00 (+1.49% on the day, +18.55% over 1 month), just 2.28% below its 52-week high of ₹8,079.50 and nearly 3x its 52-week low of ₹2,690.70 [28]. Two sessions later, the live TradingView snapshot on November 25, 2026 recorded a sharp -3.38% pullback to ₹7,628.00 (-5.59% from the 52-week high) on 80,454 shares (1.08x 30-day average volume) [28]. Across both dates, every primary moving average remains stacked in bullish order: the rising 50-day SMA (₹7,093.62 ledger / ₹7,131.09 live TV) sits well above the 200-day SMA (₹5,886.09 / ₹5,932.40), while the weekly 10-week EMA (₹7,259.37 ledger / ₹7,350.97 live TV) climbs steadily above the 30-week SMA (₹6,801.58 live TV) [28].

web_blocks.takeaway: On the verified 2026-11-23 close of ₹7,895.00, GRWRHITECH sat +8.76% above its 10W EMA (extended). The live Nov 25 pullback to ₹7,628.00 brought price to the top of our ₹7,250–₹7,650 support zone, but 4H momentum (RSI 47.47, below 4H EMA20 ₹7,707.97) has not turned up yet.

web_blocks.html: Institutional sponsorship continues to validate the Stage 2 structure. Between September 2025 and September 2026, promoter ownership held steady at 60.73% while FII ownership rose from 3.58% to 4.60% and DII ownership expanded from 4.96% to 7.27% [1]. Combined institutional stake climbed 333 bps as public retail share fell from 30.74% to 27.41% [1]. Management also maintained active global institutional outreach, hosting a 1-on-1 investor meeting with SPARX Asset Management (Hong Kong) on November 19, 2026 [35]. Meanwhile, the broader Indian market regime as of November 23, 2026 sits in an Uptrend (narrow breadth) on Nifty 50—with 55.2% of Nifty 500 stocks above their 50-day SMA, 48.2% above their 200-day SMA, 3 distribution days in 25 sessions, and 7 of 11 sectors above key moving averages [26][27].

Multi-timeframe analysis (1W / 1D / 4H) explains why patience still wins. On the verified November 23 ledger close of ₹7,895.00, GRWRHITECH was stretched +8.76% above its 10-week EMA (₹7,259.37) and +11.30% above its 50-day SMA (₹7,093.62)—outside our No-FOMO buy window and offering only 1.13:1 R:R to ₹9,300. The live November 25 drop of -3.38% to ₹7,628.00 relieved that excess, cooling Daily RSI from 63.24 to 53.65 and bringing price right onto the 20-day EMA (₹7,590.01) and top edge of our ₹7,250–₹7,650 support zone [28]. Crucially, however, the 4-hour chart has not turned up: live price sits below the 4H EMA20 (₹7,707.97) with 4H RSI at 47.47 and immediate 4H SMA50 support lower at ₹7,416.79 [28]. Waiting for either a confirmed 4H reversal above ₹7,708 or a quiet test of the 4H SMA50 / 10W EMA cluster (₹7,250–₹7,420) avoids catching a falling single-session bar.

Upward-Only Stop-Loss Ratchet (₹6,520 → ₹6,650): Because the Zerodha portfolio now holds a 1-share tracking position in GRWRHITECH, our stop-loss discipline is strictly upward-only. Since our prior November 16 dossier (stop ₹6,520.00), the rising 30-week SMA climbed from ₹6,686.88 to ₹6,801.58, matching the 20-day swing low at ₹6,801.00 [28]. TradingView's live structural stop model now sits at ₹6,646.43. We therefore ratchet our hard invalidation stop upward by +₹130 to ₹6,650.00—preserving a clean ~2.2% buffer below the ₹6,801 weekly shelf while protecting capital if Stage 2 breaks.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed why valuation requires patience, Chapter 8 reads the multi-timeframe tape to define exact execution levels. Pull up NSE:GRWRHITECH across the weekly, daily, and four-hour charts, and you see a textbook Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend undergoing a healthy, high-velocity digestion right beneath its ₹8,079.50 peak.

Start with the verified November 23, 2026 ledger close of ₹7,895.00. At that session close, GRWRHITECH was up 18.55% in a single month, trading just 2.28% below its 52-week high and nearly triple its ₹2,690.70 low. Every major moving average was aligned in bullish order: the 50-day SMA at ₹7,093.62 rode high above the 200-day SMA at ₹5,886.09, and the 10-week EMA sat at ₹7,259.37. Shareholding data confirms institutional sponsorship behind that climb: over the past year, FIIs lifted their stake from 3.58% to 4.60% and DIIs grew from 4.96% to 7.27%, absorbing 333 basis points of supply from retail holders while promoter ownership stayed locked at 60.73%.

Yet the November 23 close of ₹7,895.00 was clearly stretched—+8.76% above the 10-week EMA and +11.30% above the 50-day SMA. Just as narrow-breadth tapes often punish extended mid-caps, the live TradingView snapshot on November 25 delivered a swift -3.38% shakeout down to ₹7,628.00 on slightly above-average volume (1.08x 30-day average). That single pullback cooled daily RSI from 63.24 down to 53.65 and cut the stock's extension above its rising 10-week EMA (now ₹7,350.97) to just +3.77%.

So why not rush in blindly on the first red day at ₹7,628.00? Look down to the four-hour chart. On the 4-hour timeframe, price sits below the 4H 20-EMA at ₹7,707.97 with 4H RSI at 47.47, and the 4H 50-SMA sits lower at ₹7,416.79. In other words, the intraday pullback has not yet printed a confirmed turn. Letting price either stabilize and reclaim the 4H 20-EMA or drift deeper into the ₹7,250–₹7,420 zone—where the 4H 50-SMA and 10-week EMA converge—keeps your entry aligned with institutional demand rather than catching a falling bar.

Equally important is our upward-only stop-loss ratchet. Because your Zerodha account now holds a 1-share starter tracking position, we never lower a structural stop. Since November 16, the rising 30-week SMA climbed from ₹6,687 to ₹6,801.58—aligning almost to the rupee with the 20-day swing low at ₹6,801.00—while TradingView's suggested invalidation stop rose to ₹6,646.43. We therefore ratchet our hard stop upward from ₹6,520 to ₹6,650. That gives the stock normal breathing room for its ₹304–₹310 daily ATR while drawing an unmistakable line beneath the 30-week moving average.

Keep the broader Indian market backdrop in mind as well. As of November 23, 2026, Nifty 50 sits in an Uptrend with narrow breadth: 55.2% of Nifty 500 names trade above their 50-day SMA, only 48.2% stand above their 200-day SMA, and the index carries 3 distribution days over the last 25 sessions. In narrow-breadth markets, leaders with 90.4th-percentile relative strength like GRWRHITECH tend to hold their 10-week EMA during pullbacks, while weaker peers roll over—which is exactly what happened to Cosmo First as it slipped below its 30-week SMA.

Finally, remember that Garware is not part of the NSE Futures and Options segment. There are no liquid calls, puts, or collars to structure leverage or hedges. Everything comes down to cash-equity discipline: protect the held starter share with a Zerodha GTT stop at ₹6,650, wait for 4-hour confirmation inside ₹7,250–₹7,650 before scaling up, and let the rising 30-week SMA carry the trend.

Map the exact levels onto your chart before the next session opens so emotions never override your plan. Overhead, pivot resistance R1 sits at ₹7,658.33, the 4-hour 20-EMA sits at ₹7,707.97, the 52-week high stands at ₹8,079.50, and pivot R2 rises to ₹8,342.17. Underneath, institutional support clusters tightly between the 20-day SMA at ₹7,581.35, the 4-hour 50-SMA at ₹7,416.79, and the rising 10-week EMA at ₹7,350.97, all resting above the 30-week SMA floor at ₹6,801.58. If GRWRHITECH absorbs the November 25 selling on lighter volume over the next several sessions and reclaims ₹7,708 on the 4-hour chart—or tests ₹7,250 to ₹7,420 and prints a higher low—your pullback setup is complete. If instead it slices through ₹6,801 and breaks ₹6,650 on heavy volume, our GTT takes us out cleanly with minimal portfolio damage.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a Stage 2 leader pulls back 3.4% off its highs toward the 20-day EMA, the temptation is to either panic or pounce immediately. Reading the 4-hour chart solves both mistakes: keep your ratcheted ₹6,650 stop in place on the starter share, and wait for 4H stabilization inside ₹7,250–₹7,650 before adding new capital.
